types.name: qttune_frame_t
types.decl:
typedef struct qttune_frame {
    uint64_t timestamp_us;    /* Microseconds since session start (producer's
                                 steady clock, monotonic per channel). The
                                 J2534 transport passes the vendor's 32-bit
                                 timestamp through instead (Known Issue #12) */
    uint32_t arbitration_id;  /* CAN identifier: <= 0x7FF standard, up to
                                 0x1FFFFFFF when FLAG_EXTENDED set */
    uint16_t channel_id;      /* Bus/channel index only — never multiplexes
                                 an arbitration ID */
    uint16_t data_length;     /* Bytes used in data[]: 0..64 */
    uint8_t  data[64];        /* Classic CAN (8) .. CAN-FD (64) payload */
    uint32_t flags;           /* QTTUNE_FRAME_FLAG_* bitmask */
    uint32_t reserved;        /* Producers MUST leave zero; ABI growth space */
} qttune_frame_t;
types.doc: Frame structure — POD only, no pointers. Layout is pinned by the assertions below: 88 bytes, no hidden padding on any supported platform (ADR-0006).

types.name: qttune_status_t
types.decl:
typedef enum {
    QT_OK = 0,
    QT_ERR_NULL_ARGUMENT = 1,
    QT_ERR_NOT_IMPLEMENTED = 2,
    QT_ERR_NO_TRANSPORT = 3,
    QT_ERR_OUT_OF_MEMORY = 4,
    QT_ERR_SESSION_CLOSED = 5,
    QT_ERR_ALREADY_REGISTERED = 6,  /* Not returned: a duplicate callback
                                       registration succeeds (pair identity,
                                       ADR-0002). Reserved, since codes are
                                       append-only */
    QT_ERR_LOAD_FAILED = 7,
    /* Link-health codes: published by the J2534 worker through
     * qttune_session_get_error_state while the session keeps running. */
    QT_ERR_VEHICLE_TIMEOUT = 8,         /* reads answer, but nothing arrives */
    QT_ERR_TRANSPORT_HARD_FAILURE = 9,  /* reads fail: the adapter isn't
                                           answering */
    QT_ERR_REQUEST_FAILED = 10,  /* writes fail while reads stay clean: no
                                    node ACKs the requests (ignition off,
                                    ECU asleep, no vehicle). The adapter is
                                    fine, so this isn't a hard failure */

    /* Append-only rule: new codes go HERE, never renumber */
} qttune_status_t;
types.doc: Status codes - append-only evolution for ABI stability

types.name: qttune_transport_ops_t
types.doc: Transport abstraction (internal): sessions own a transport instance polymorphically. ops is a pointer to static, immutable vtable storage owned by the transport implementation TU; impl is the implementation's private state. Both start() and detach() are invoked by the session, never by transports themselves — no re-entry into session lifecycle. Contract: - start(): called from qttune_session_start. Must be idempotent (second call on a running transport returns QT_OK). - detach(): called exactly once from qttune_session_close, AFTER the closed flag is set. Must stop any worker threads and free impl + the qttune_transport wrapper itself. May not touch session afterwards.

types.name: qttune_pid_scheduler
types.doc: Round-robin PID scheduler (ADR-0013). Fixed capacity, no allocation, owned exclusively by the transport worker thread — single-threaded by construction, so no synchronization inside. PID derivation rule: a def drives scheduling iff it has a 2-byte mux key at payload offset 0 — the [41][PID] echo that opens a Mode-01 response once the transport strips the address header. The PID to request is the key's low byte. Sets without such defs (raw, mock) enroll nothing, and the worker falls back to ?poll= or passive receive. Nothing validates this shape at registration, so from_set() checks it itself.
